segments.title: Introduction and Snake Rag with King Oliver
segments.summary: Gleason introduces Armstrong and plays Snake Rag from the 1923 King Oliver Creole Jazz Band record.

segments.title: Arriving in Oliver's band and how it differed from New Orleans
segments.summary: Armstrong recalls feeling not good enough at the door, the band's setup versus New Orleans, the repertoire, and going straight to work as second cornet with no rehearsal.

segments.title: Making Snake Rag: rehearsing, balance and no drums on early records
segments.summary: Armstrong explains the band rehearsed on the job, records were cut quickly, lead was lost, drums were avoided, and he improvised breaks to Oliver's cues.

segments.title: Admiring Oliver and playing second cornet
segments.summary: Armstrong says it was a big thing to be sent for by Oliver, whom he admired; he had few solos and did not yet sing.

segments.title: Blues singers and Ma Rainey's Countin' the Blues
segments.summary: Gleason introduces a Ma Rainey record; Armstrong says singers like Bessie, Mamie and Clara Smith played theaters rather than Oliver's Lincoln Gardens.

segments.title: Accompanying blues singers on record
segments.summary: Armstrong describes how he got the accompanying work through Fletcher Henderson and how he filled in behind singers, recalling Bessie Smith writing blues in the studio.

segments.title: Ma Rainey, Bessie Smith and other blues singers
segments.summary: Armstrong compares Ma Rainey and Bessie Smith and says he played with all of the blues singers.

segments.title: The Hot Five, Skid-Dat-De-Dat and early scatting
segments.summary: Gleason notes the Hot Five records were made in a short period; Armstrong says he named the group for recording, made up tunes in the studio, and scatting came from New Orleans quartets.

segments.title: Writing down the Hot Five tunes and which ones were played live
segments.summary: Armstrong says New Orleans musicians needed no written parts and that only the popular tunes were played regularly.

segments.title: Varied band experience and advice to young musicians
segments.summary: Armstrong lists Erskine Tate at the Vendome, Fletcher Henderson, Fate Marable's boat band, Joe Glaser at the Sunset and Carroll Dickerson, and advises youngsters to play with good musicians.

segments.title: Closing with Mack the Knife
segments.summary: Gleason closes the program with Mack the Knife by the All-Stars.
